summary: The entry contains two I headings with different lexemes. All additions are keyed by stem_id, so disgust 1 and squishing 1 cannot be confused despite identical stem labels.

Disgust consistently takes lebe/lebayye as subject, a possessor as experiencer and m-/min- stimulus. A possessed heart with plural possessors does not by itself prove that the heart noun is morphologically plural.

The disgust forms are lexically Detransitive, with no expressed causer; German translations often suppress the heart subject. Preterit mgawlaʕ can describe a current resulting feeling; Infectum also has prospective g-.

The squishing tokens have active participants: people work clay with their hands, dogs affect a boy. Retaining the inherited Detransitive box is a filing choice pending paradigm review, not evidence that those actors are affected themes.
Allowed glvč lookup has mgalvačle/mgalvəč and a narrower food-dirtying meaning; gwl has mixing forms. Neither establishes a safe automatic root merger or new root for the present variants.
No new numbered lexical sense is necessary: clay manipulation and mangling fit the already supplied squishing subentry, and all disgust examples fit its inherited sole sense.
Should the inherited Gwlč material be separated under a confirmed headword, and what is its relationship to glvč? Do not merge it with disgust simply because both are parsed as I.
Confirm the diathesis and exact suffix segmentation of mgawlčíwaynale and mgavlačče, and whether l/v order is a regular variant.
Does the Detransitive-only filing for mgawlč represent a deponent paradigm or an inherited heading error? Existing kmgawlčo u muklo already has an actor and object.
Does disgust lebayye mean a collective/shared heart or plural hearts? The singular verb and plural possessor alone do not settle number.
Supply translations for the inherited mud/snow/floor personal-communication examples before publishing a revised translated version of them.
Squishing applies to clay being worked and to a boy being mangled, extending participants beyond the inherited food/mud contexts.
